news.full_article_text: Whole areas of Derna have been entirely rebuilt - Published 16 November 2026, 00:11 GMT "It was joy when I moved in. I could finally relax," says Abdulwahab Damdoum, surveying his luxurious new apartment overlooking the Mediterranean Sea, in the eastern Libyan city of Derna. Just three years ago he was clinging in terror to the roof of a house as the world's deadliest flood this century surged around him. Now the 27-year-old port worker, his wife and two young daughters have been given a new, free, 300-sq-m home in a showcase development commissioned by a son of Khalifa Haftar, the warlord who controls eastern Libya. It is part of a rapid $2bn (Â£1.5bn) rebuilding of Derna that the powerful Haftar family hope will serve as a model for development throughout Libya, increasing their influence across a country currently split between east and west, with rival governments in charge. The money comes from the state coffers of the oil-rich country, allocated by its parliament. But there are no published records of how it has been spent, raising questions about accountability and possible corruption. Damdoum, like many flood survivors, simply thanks the head of the Development and Reconstruction Fund, Belkacem Haftar, for what has been achieved since the early hours of 11 September 2023, when lashing rain from Storm Daniel burst two dams above Derna, sending a wall of water 7m (23 ft) high cascading down onto the sleeping city. The exact death toll will probably never be known. Some estimates have been as high as 6,000, though 4,000 now seems a more likely figure. Many bodies are still unidentified. Abdulwahab Damdoum lost his father, brother and sister in the flood In a city of about 100,000 people, that means almost everybody lost someone they loved. The 14 relatives and neighbours on the roof with Damdoum â including his father, brother and sister - all drowned. He survived, but his home was destroyed, and he had to find temporary accommodation. "It was rent, rent, rent," he says. "Now, no-one can take this [new flat] from me. I thank Engineer Belkacem. God sent this person who picked the city up from disaster." Portraits of Belkacem, widely known simply as "the Engineer", his younger brother Saddam, a military chief also involved in reconstruction, and their father Khalifa are on hoardings all over Derna and the region. "Since 2011, Libya has not built big projects like this," says Hussein el-Mansory, project manager of the "2,000 Apartments" complex where Damdoum now lives. "I feel very happy and proud and I'll tell my children: 'I made this.'" The complex includes a new mosque, hospital, shopping mall and schools. New roads, bridges have also been built in Derna. But while many survivors have been rehoused, some are still waiting. Among them is Izz al-Nasr Ibzeou, a marine science lecturer at the university. His wife Salima, her mother Mouna, and all the couple's seven children, aged between one and 11, drowned. His family home was ruined, but the authorities have not yet fully restored it because Ibzeou also has an undamaged apartment in another part of town. He returns every day to his old house, now an empty shell, to see his children's possessions, which he has kept in dust-covered piles. "This is my son Moez's bike. He played with it every day. And this is my daughter Fawzia's dress. She wore it whenever she went to a wedding," Ibzeou says. "Even if I decide not to come to remember them, my feet will bring me here of their own accord." To this day, he has not found their bodies. In Derna's vast new flood cemetery, most graves are marked only by numbers, not names, because the process of matching survivors' DNA with corpses is still not completed. "I go to the cemetery and try to guess where my family are," he says. "This has burned my heart too much. Thank God, I'm patient, but I'm still waiting just to read the Qur'an [at their graves] and say hello to them." Izz al-Nasr Ibzeou visits his former home every day, to remember his children Belkacem Haftar has now extended the work of his reconstruction fund to Libya's second city, Benghazi, and other parts of Libya his father controls. Officials have talked in the past about turning the city into a version of "Dubai on the Mediterranean." Who owns Libya's future? Tim Whewell reports from eastern Libya, where a vast reconstruction programme led by the Haftar family is transforming cities and reshaping the country's political future. Belkacem tells the BBC he has accomplished more than any previous Libyan administration. "Libya went through the Gaddafi era, 40 years of neglect and poverty," he said. "The interim governments [post-Gaddafi, based in Tripoli] wasted a lot of money without providing anything the people could touch. I have never made promises to the people. But I have provided them with what they need." International human rights organisations have repeatedly accused the authorities in eastern Libya and Libyan Arab Armed Forces headed by Khalifa Haftar of serious abuses, including secret executions, arbitrary detentions and forced disappearances. The Haftars and the Benghazi-based government deny the allegations. Belkacem told the BBC there was complete freedom of speech in eastern Libya. news.full_article_text: Donald Trump greeting Jensen Huang in September this year - Published 16 November 2026, 11:45 GMT Nvidia has dismissed a campaign calling for Jensen Huang to be handed back his job as allies, including US President Donald Trump, backed the effort. Trump said on Monday that he "would certainly not mind" if Huang was reinstated, adding to a list of supporters who are backing a "Bring Jensen Back" campaign. Fellow tech bosses, including SpaceX's Elon Musk and Tim Sweeney, chief executive of Fortnite-maker Epic Games, have also supported Huang's return. But the BBC has been told the board of the AI chip giant is not interested in bringing him back after he resigned last week following revelations he had two affairs, including one that involved a suspected Chinese spy. Meanwhile on Monday, the Trump administration said it will further restrict China's âaccess to AI chips from companies like Nvidia. The reported affairs created a crisis for one of the world's most valuable firms - a central company in AI and the US battle against China for dominance. Since his departure, supporters have launched an online petition demanding his return. Musk and Sweeny are among the more than 175,000 who have signed the open letter calling for the board to reinstate Huang while an ongoing internal probe is conducted. The "Stand with Jensen" campaign claims to have been launched by a make up of current and former Nvidia employees, partners, shareholders and supporters, all demanding the return of the former chief executive. They expressed concerns the ex-Nvidia boss "was removed without meaningful due process". President Trump gave his views on Huang's future on Monday, saying he "would certainly not mind" seeing the former boss given his job back. "I guess maybe one lesson is more important than another, but I would certainly not mind seeing that," he told reporters as he left the White House. The Trump administration on Monday also issued new restrictions on chip exports to overseas data centres, which allow Chinese companies to access advanced AI chips to train AI models. The move came ahead of Trump's meeting with Chinese President Xi Jingping this week. The new rules will require companies in Singapore, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia and Brazil to apply for US export licences for the most advanced chips in an effort to cut down on them being illegally diverted to China. Huang had been expected to weather the storm following the revelation of an affair involving Alice Huang, alleged to be a Chinese spy. However, he resigned last Thursday after a second extra-marital relationship emerged, allegedly with an executive at Nvidia who reported to him. The scandal-hit tech boss was discussing a possible return to Nvidia with confidants, according to the Financial Times , external , though Nvidia's board is not considering reappointing him. A representative for Huang declined to comment on the report. The so-called war room also wants to get support for Huang from the White House. President Trump has spoken in glowing terms about Huang since the scandal erupted, and also said he believed Huang when the former Nvidia boss told him he had "no idea she was a spy". Trump's view is at odds with his Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, who has called for Nvidia to hire its next chief executive from outside the company. The scandal has created tensions between the US Treasury and Commerce departments over shipments of high-end Nvidia chips to Alice Huang's former firm, Megaspeed. China has denied that Alice Huang is a spy. It has raised questions about the possibility that the chips may have ended up in China despite US export restrictions. 'China plays games with us, so we play games with China' On Monday, Trump said he did not know whether the women Huang had an affair with was a spy for China. "They say she's a spy. I don't know that she was a spy at all. I mean, I really don't, I don't know that," he said. Huang has agreed to testify in Congress, including before the House Select Committee on China to discuss whether US national security was compromised by his affair. Trump said he did not think Huang had put national security at risk. "You know, China plays games with us. So we play games with China," he said. The FBI is also investigating the affair between the former Nvidia boss and Alice Huang, according to Trump. 'A handshake with Jensen' Musk claimed that "critical deals" involving Nvidia's technology would be lost following Huang's resignation. "Jensen drove supply chain brilliantly at Nvidia but many of those deals were a handshake with Jensen, not a written contract," he posted on X. , external "Without Jensen, at least some of those critical deals will be lost." Fellow tech boss Sam Altman, the chief executive of OpenAI, sidestepped the question of Huang returning to Nvidia at a conference, saying: "I don't think I know enough to answer that question." But Altman, who himself was reinstated to his job after being fired back in 2023, said Huang was a "hero of mine". Shareholders in Nvidia also want Huang back at the company's helm. Hundreds of billions of pounds have been wiped off the firm's stock market value in recent days, but it is still worth some $3.87 trillion. Its share price was down in early Monday trading. In an open letter to the board, Brad Gerstner, founder of Altimeter Capital and Atreides Management boss Gavin Baker called for management to leave "all options on the table, including the potential return of Jensen Huang". Lord Sarfraz, a member of the UK's House of Lords, has also written to Nvidia's new chair, Harvey Jones, urging the firm's directors to give "serious consideration" to Huang's return following the investigation. For the moment, Nvidia's chief financial officer Colette Kress is leading the firm and will present the company's results on Tuesday. news.full_article_text: What happens next in Yemen may send fresh shockwaves to the world economy - Published 47 minutes ago The Iran-backed Houthi rebels who seized much of Yemen in 2014 have now forced the army of the internationally recognised government to withdraw from the Red Sea coast in order to defend their interim capital, Aden. Their advance bodes ill for Yemen's legitimate, internationally recognised government, its Saudi backers and, by extension, much of the rest of the world. Yemen, a mountainous, heavily armed, intensely tribal and largely impoverished nation, sits at the far south-west corner of the Arabian Peninsula. The country has two coasts: One faces the Indian Ocean on which sits the once-prosperous trading port of Aden, the other faces the Red Sea and, most importantly, the narrow chokepoint at the southern exit of that waterway - the so-called Bab al-Mandab Strait or, in English, The Gate of Tears. Whoever controls that strait can threaten any or all maritime traffic passing through from both the Mediterranean and the Red Sea to the Indian Ocean. In normal times, it accounts for around 12% of global trade, with anywhere between 70 to 150 ships a day making the transit. But not any more. Although the Houthis say they are no threat to maritime traffic, they are currently at war with Saudi Arabia, making it extremely hazardous for the Saudis to send their oil tankers past the now rebel-controlled coast. Watch: Why is the Bab al-Mandab Strait so important? When the US and Israel started a war with Iran in February, Tehran responded by choking off much of the oil trade flowing out of the Gulf through another narrow chokepoint - the Strait of Hormuz. This sent oil prices soaring, boosted inflation and hurt economies everywhere. The Saudis had a Plan B. Instead of exporting their oil past the dangerous coast of Iran, where their tankers risked being droned or mined by Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps, they started pumping it overland through their East-West Pipeline to an export terminal on the Red Sea at Yanbu. This worked for a while. But then in July a cold truce between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis broke down, that pipeline got hit by drones and the rebels started firing missiles and drones at targets all over Saudi Arabia. On land, the Houthis seized the initiative and made a lightning dash down the Red Sea coast, sending the Yemeni army into headlong retreat. A brief counter-offensive appears to have failed and the Houthis are now reported to be in full control of the Bab al-Mandab Strait and the nearby offshore islands. Nicholas Hopton, a former British Ambassador to both Yemen and Iran and now director-general of the UK-based Middle East Association, says: "The decision by the legitimate government of Yemen to prioritise the military defence of Aden at the expense of withdrawing from other areas suggests that the war is not going well for the Saudi-backed [Yemeni] government. And the rest of the world should be worried." He warns that if the port of Aden â a city of roughly 1.25 million inhabitants â was to fall to the Houthis, it "would undoubtedly precipitate a further escalation in the regional crisis and further fragility in the global economy, catalysed by the US-Iran war". But Mohammed al-Basha, the Yemeni founder of the US-based risk advisory firm Basha Report, believes the Houthis would struggle to capture the heavily fortified city of Aden. "Any attempt to seize a densely populated city like Aden would come at a significant human cost," Basha said. "Advancing across the flat coastal plains would also expose Houthi forces to air power." "For now, the Houthis appear to be seeking a negotiated surrender, hoping to exploit infighting and divisions among southern factions to achieve their objectives without a costly urban offensive." It is conceivable that the Yemen war will settle into a less dramatic but deeply unsatisfactory stasis - a situation where casualty figures subside yet the country remains split between areas controlled by the Houthis - Iran's Shia allies - and the disparate and often poorly motivated forces of the Saudi-backed Yemeni army. The former British defence attachÃ© to Yemen, Col Iain Smailes, warned that the recent Houthi advance could trigger a spike in oil prices, as it did when they seized the Bab al-Mandab Strait in September. He also warns this could have a knock-on effect to security well beyond Yemen's borders. "By extending their control over the western coastline, the Houthis will increase their ability to smuggle weapons and ammunition from Iran, the Horn of Africa and elsewhere, posing additional threats to the region," Col Smailes said. "This control will enable both Iran and the Houthis to extend their influence in East Africa and beyond." news.headline: Major US Banks and Zelle Suffer Online Access Disruptions Following Global Microsoft Outage
news.story_lead: Customers across several major United States financial institutions—including Bank of America, Chase, JP Morgan, Wells Fargo, and digital payment platform Zelle—reported widespread issues accessing their online accounts. The banking disruptions followed a major global outage affecting Microsoft services.
news.full_article_text:
US Banking Disruptions Following Global IT Outage

Customers of leading American financial institutions, including Bank of America, Chase, JP Morgan, and Wells Fargo, along with the digital payment platform Zelle, experienced significant online service disruptions on November 17, 2026. Users encountered errors and technical barriers while attempting to log into their online banking portals and mobile applications.

The widespread disruption in critical financial operations occurred immediately following a major global IT outage associated with Microsoft infrastructure. The incident highlighted the digital interdependence of major commercial banking operations and digital payment networks on core technology infrastructure.
news.background_context: The online account access issues across major US banks and Zelle coincided directly with a major global service outage at Microsoft.

The incident highlights operational resilience concerns within critical financial infrastructure.

hindi_translation.story_lead: बैंक ऑफ अमेरिका, चेस, जेपी मॉर्गन, वेल्स फार्गो और डिजिटल भुगतान प्लेटफॉर्म जेल (Zelle) सहित कई प्रमुख अमेरिकी वित्तीय संस्थानों के ग्राहकों ने अपने ऑनलाइन खातों तक पहुंच में समस्या की रिपोर्ट की। यह बैंकिंग व्यवधान माइक्रोसॉफ्ट की सेवाओं में बड़े पैमाने पर हुए वैश्विक आउटेज के बाद दर्ज किया गया।

news.headline: Yamuna River Pollution Increases Despite Massive Cleaning Funds; Supreme Court Mandates Strict CPCB Monitoring and State Penalties
news.story_lead: The Supreme Court of India expressed severe concern over the deteriorating water quality of the Yamuna River, noting that pollution levels have continued to rise despite substantial public expenditure on river rejuvenation. A division bench of Justices Manoj Misra and Manmohan directed the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) to establish point-wise water monitoring and impose financial penalties on administrative units where water quality degrades.
news.full_article_text:
### Supreme Court Directives on Yamuna Pollution Framework

The Supreme Court of India has held that the poor health of the Yamuna River directly reflects widespread failures in municipal administration across cities, towns, and villages situated along its banks. In its order dated November 4, a bench comprising Justice Manoj Misra and Justice Manmohan observed that approximately 520 drains currently discharge wastewater directly into the Yamuna. The court underlined that constructing additional Sewage Treatment Plants (STPs) alone will not solve the crisis unless industrial effluents and untreated sewage are intercepted and stopped at their source.

### Monitoring Mandate and Financial Penalties

To enforce institutional accountability, the apex court directed the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) to systematically monitor water quality at all points where the Yamuna River and its major drains enter and exit states, Union Territories (UTs), and districts. If water quality degrades on any parameter while flowing through or exiting a jurisdiction, the responsible state, UT, or district authority will be held accountable and penalised. The fines collected must be deposited directly with the Supreme Court Registry, and CPCB has been tasked with developing a standardized formula to calculate compensation.

### Structural Obstacles in Urban Sewage Management

The court highlighted critical structural bottlenecks in urban waste management, pointing out that tapping sewage remains a severe challenge due to the lack of robust sewerage networks and the improper merging of stormwater drains with sewage lines. Furthermore, civic authorities face practical impossibilities in laying sewage pipelines in illegal, unauthorized colonies and 'jhuggi-jhopdi' (slum) clusters built on encroached land due to non-grid layouts and lack of spatial clearance. The bench emphasized that unless such unauthorized settlements along riverbeds and major drains are cleared and occupants rehabilitated, untreated domestic waste will continue to pollute the river.

### Inspection Rights and Incident Investigations

The Supreme Court mandated that all public and private entities, plant operators, concessionaires, and waste management agencies grant CPCB and its designated third-party agencies immediate, unhindered, and unconditional access to facilities at any hour. This includes surprise sample collection, unannounced inspections, volumetric audits, and sensor verifications. In addition, CPCB must investigate and submit detailed reports on specific pollution events—such as mass fish deaths, floating toxic white foam, eutrophication, algal blooms, or sudden spikes in Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD), Chemical Oxygen Demand (COD), and Total Suspended Solids (TSS) levels. All central and state ministries and agencies have been ordered to extend full logistical, technical, and operational assistance to CPCB. The matter is set for its next hearing on January 13.

hindi_translation.story_lead: सर्वोच्च न्यायालय ने यमुना नदी की स्थिति पर गहरी चिंता व्यक्त करते हुए कहा है कि भारी धनराशि खर्च किए जाने के बावजूद प्रदूषण बढ़ा है। न्यायमूर्ति मनोज मिश्रा और न्यायमूर्ति मनमोहन की पीठ ने केंद्रीय प्रदूषण नियंत्रण बोर्ड (सीपीसीबी) को राज्यों, केंद्र शासित प्रदेशों और जिलों के प्रवेश और निकास बिंदुओं पर जल गुणवत्ता की निगरानी करने तथा गुणवत्ता बिगड़ने पर जुर्माने के आदेश दिए हैं।
hindi_translation.full_article_text:
### यमुना प्रदूषण पर सर्वोच्च न्यायालय का सख्त रुख

सर्वोच्च न्यायालय ने माना है कि यमुना नदी के किनारे बसे शहरों, कस्बों और गांवों के नागरिक प्रशासन की विफलताएं नदी के खराब स्वास्थ्य में दिखाई देती हैं। 4 नवंबर के अपने आदेश में न्यायमूर्ति मनोज मिश्रा और न्यायमूर्ति मनमोहन की पीठ ने पाया कि लगभग 520 नाले सीधे यमुना में अनुपचारित अपशिष्ट जल गिराते हैं। अदालत ने जोर देकर कहा कि केवल नए सीवेज ट्रीटमेंट प्लांट (एसटीपी) बनाना पर्याप्त नहीं है, जब तक कि औद्योगिक प्रदूषकों और अनुपचारित सीवेज को स्रोत पर ही नहीं रोका जाता।

### सीपीसीबी की निगरानी और वित्तीय जुर्माने का ढांचा

प्रशासनिक जवाबदेही तय करने के लिए शीर्ष अदालत ने केंद्रीय प्रदूषण नियंत्रण बोर्ड (सीपीसीबी) को निर्देश दिया कि वह राज्यों, केंद्र शासित प्रदेशों और जिलों के प्रवेश और निकास बिंदुओं पर जल गुणवत्ता की निगरानी करे। यदि किसी क्षेत्र से गुजरते समय पानी की गुणवत्ता में गिरावट आती है, तो संबंधित प्राधिकारी को जिम्मेदार ठहराया जाएगा और उस पर जुर्माना लगाया जाएगा। यह जुर्माना सुप्रीम कोर्ट की रजिस्ट्री में जमा होगा, और सीपीसीबी को जुर्माने की गणना के लिए सूत्र तैयार करने का काम सौंपा गया है।

### शहरी कचरा प्रबंधन की संरचनात्मक चुनौतियां

अदालत ने कहा कि ठोस सीवेज नेटवर्क की कमी और वर्षा जल नालों के सीवेज लाइनों में मिलने के कारण सीवेज को रोकना एक बड़ी चुनौती है। इसके अलावा, अतिक्रमण की गई भूमि पर बनी अवैध और अनधिकृत कॉलोनियों तथा झुग्गी-झोपड़ी बस्तियों में सीवेज लाइन बिछाने के लिए जगह और ग्रिड लेआउट नहीं है। जब तक इन बस्तियों को हटाकर पुनर्वास नहीं किया जाता, तब तक अनुपचारित कचरा नदी को दूषित करता रहेगा।

### औचक निरीक्षण और प्रदूषण घटनाओं की जांच

सर्वोच्च न्यायालय ने निर्देश दिया कि सभी सार्वजनिक और निजी अपशिष्ट प्रबंधन एजेंसियों को सीपीसीबी और उसके नामित निकायों को 24 घंटे औचक निरीक्षण, नमूना संग्रह और ऑडिट के लिए बिना शर्त पहुंच प्रदान करनी होगी। इसके अलावा, मछली की मौत, सफेद झाग बनने, यूट्रोफिकेशन (शैवाल प्रसार), तथा बीओडी (BOD), सीओडी (COD), और टीएसएस (TSS) के स्तर में वृद्धि जैसी घटनाओं पर सीपीसीबी को विस्तृत जांच रिपोर्ट प्रस्तुत करनी होगी। मामले की अगली सुनवाई 13 जनवरी को होगी।

news.headline: INDIA Bloc Moves Supreme Court Seeking Sworn Responses from ECI on 48 Questions Regarding Electoral Roll Revision
news.story_lead: Opposition leaders led by Rahul Gandhi have petitioned the Supreme Court to seek formal affidavits from top Election Commission of India officials regarding 48 questions on the nationwide Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The petition raises questions over internal decision-making, reported dissent among commissioners, data centralisation, and changes to online voter registration forms.
news.full_article_text:
### Supreme Court Petition on ECI Decision-Making

Opposition leaders from the INDIA bloc, including Rahul Gandhi, have approached the Supreme Court seeking permission to direct key officials of the Election Commission of India (ECI) to respond under oath to 48 detailed queries. The petition requests individual sworn affidavits from Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, as well as the ECI's Director General (IT).

### Key Areas of Inquiry Raised by the Petitioners

1. **Authorization and Internal Dissent:** The petitioners have sought details on who ordered the nationwide Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise, the specific file records, dates of approval, and individual opinions of panel members. They specifically asked for records of objections or disagreements voiced by Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi concerning SIR, ECINET, Form 6, and appeal filings.
2. **Counter-Affidavit & Approvals:** The petition challenges the ECI's counter-affidavit claiming unanimous decisions, pointing out the absence of recorded dates, file numbers, or meeting minutes. It seeks clarification on whether electronic media like WhatsApp or emails were used for official approvals and whether such records have been archived.
3. **Administrative Orders & Centralisation:** Queries have been raised regarding the delegation of powers to the Chief Election Commissioner, centralisation of ERONET and ECINET, authorization of the office order dated July 28, 2026, and whether the CEC concurred with a joint directive issued by the two Election Commissioners on July 30, 2026.
4. **Form 6 Declaration & Exclusions:** The petition questions the introduction of an additional declaration in online Form 6 without clear formal authorization dates, asking how many applications were rejected or kept pending due to non-submission of this declaration or mapping details. It also requests state-wise and gender-wise data on voter exclusions across pre-SIR, draft, and final rolls.
5. **West Bengal Appeals & Form 7 Usage:** Information has been sought regarding ECI's decisions to appeal against West Bengal judicial officers' orders that allowed voter inclusions, as well as actions taken under Section 31 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950 regarding false or excessive objections filed via Form 7.

### निर्वाचन आयोग के निर्णय लेने की प्रक्रिया पर सर्वोच्च न्यायालय में याचिका

राहुल गांधी सहित इंडिया ब्लॉक के विपक्षी नेताओं ने सर्वोच्च न्यायालय का रुख कर भारत निर्वाचन आयोग (ECI) के प्रमुख अधिकारियों को 48 विस्तृत प्रश्नों के उत्तर शपथ पत्र के माध्यम से देने का निर्देश देने की मांग की है। याचिका में मुख्य निर्वाचन आयुक्त ज्ञानेश कुमार, निर्वाचन आयुक्त सुखबीर सिंह संधू और विवेक जोशी, तथा ECI के महानिदेशक (IT) से व्यक्तिगत हलफनामे मांगे गए हैं।

### याचिकाकर्ताओं द्वारा उठाए गए मुख्य विषय

1. **स्वीकृति और आंतरिक असहमति:** याचिकाकर्ताओं ने पूछा है कि राष्ट्रव्यापी विशेष गहन संशोधन (SIR) का आदेश किसने दिया, फाइल रिकॉर्ड, निर्णय की तारीखें और पैनल के सदस्यों की व्यक्तिगत राय क्या थी। उन्होंने सुखबीर सिंह संधू और विवेक जोशी द्वारा SIR, ECINET, फॉर्म 6 और अपीलों को लेकर दर्ज कराई गई आपत्तियों की जानकारी मांगी है।
2. **काउंटर-हलफनामा और स्वीकृतियां:** याचिका में आयोग के उस हलफनामे को चुनौती दी गई है जिसमें फैसलों को सर्वसम्मत बताया गया है, परंतु फाइल नंबर या बैठक के मिनट्स प्रस्तुत नहीं किए गए हैं। इसमें पूछा गया है कि क्या आधिकारिक मंजूरी के लिए व्हाट्सएप या ईमेल का उपयोग किया गया था।
3. **प्रशासनिक आदेश और केंद्रीकरण:** मुख्य निर्वाचन आयुक्त को शक्तियों के प्रत्यायोजन, ERONET और ECINET के केंद्रीकरण, 28 जुलाई 2026 के कार्यालय आदेश, और 30 जुलाई 2026 को दो चुनाव आयुक्तों द्वारा जारी संयुक्त निर्देश पर CEC की सहमति के संबंध में सवाल पूछे गए हैं।
4. **फॉर्म 6 में संशोधन और नाम हटाना:** बिना औपचारिक मंजूरी के ऑनलाइन फॉर्म 6 में अतिरिक्त घोषणा जोड़ने और इसके कारण लंबित या खारिज हुए आवेदनों की संख्या पूछी गई है।
5. **पश्चिम बंगाल में अपीलें एवं फॉर्म 7 का उपयोग:** पश्चिम बंगाल के न्यायिक अधिकारियों के आदेशों के खिलाफ ECI द्वारा दायर अपीलों और लोक प्रतिनिधित्व अधिनियम, 1950 की धारा 31 के तहत झूठी फॉर्म 7 आपत्तियों पर की गई कार्रवाई की जानकारी मांगी गई है।
